indices.subtitle: Basic covers index notation, powers, squares and square and cube roots, prime factors and factor trees, and the first index laws with the zero index. Expected adds prime factorisation in index form, HCF and LCM, estimating roots, order of operations, showing why the index laws work, and the index laws with pronumerals.

ratios-rates.subtitle: Basic covers simplifying and equivalent ratios, a ratio as a fraction, sharing in a ratio, unit rates and reading and drawing distance–time graphs. Expected adds ratios with units, three-part ratios, ratio problems from one part or a difference, scale, converting rates, best buys, speed, distance and time, and drawing and interpreting distance–time graphs with a return journey.

linear.subtitle: Basic covers reading and plotting points and quadrants, tables of values, matching rules, completing a table and drawing the line, and solving an equation by drawing graphs. Expected adds rules from tables and graphs, patterns, real-life relationships, lines in all four quadrants, and graphical solutions and points of intersection.

area.subtitle: Basic covers rectangles, triangles and parallelograms (including drawing shapes with a given area), missing lengths, the area of a circle in terms of π and choosing units. Expected adds trapeziums (and why the formula works), rhombuses and kites, circles, sectors, semicircles and quadrants, composite shapes, working backwards and converting units of area.

volume.subtitle: Basic covers views of solids (choose and draw), prisms, counting cubes, V = Ah, rectangular prisms and units of volume and capacity. Expected adds drawing top, front and side views, triangular, trapezium and composite prisms, cylinders, missing dimensions, capacity and converting units.

geometrical-figures.subtitle: Basic covers classifying and sketching triangles and quadrilaterals, their properties, and the angle sums of triangles and quadrilaterals. Expected adds classifying by sides and angles together, which triangles are possible, isosceles and exterior angles, the quadrilateral family, convex and non-convex polygons, and angles and sides found from properties.

data-visualisation.subtitle: Basic covers categorical and numerical data, frequency tables, drawing column graphs and dot plots, and reading column graphs, dot plots, pictograms and line graphs. Expected adds classifying variables fully, census, sample and bias, choosing a display, drawing stem-and-leaf plots and histograms, and reading stem-and-leaf plots, histograms, sector and divided bar graphs and misleading graphs.

data-analysis.subtitle: Basic covers the mean, median, mode and range (alone and together), the mean in context, the effect of a new value, and statistics from a dot plot. Expected adds even-sized data sets, the mean to 1 decimal place, missing values, outliers and changing data, frequency tables, stem-and-leaf plots, the shape of a distribution, comparing data sets and choosing a measure of centre.

probability.subtitle: Basic covers chance words, the 0 to 1 scale, sample spaces, dice, spinners, bags and cards, and P(A) with P(not A). Expected adds probabilities as fractions, decimals and percentages, letters, outcomes that are not equally likely, relative frequency (and explaining it), expected numbers and complementary events.

pythagoras.subtitle: Basic covers the hypotenuse, writing Pythagoras' theorem, squares and square roots, testing for a right angle, and finding the hypotenuse (with and without a diagram). Expected adds Pythagorean triads, answers to 1 decimal place, shorter sides, mixed units, isosceles triangles and problems in context where students draw the diagram.

angle-relationships.subtitle: Basic covers classifying and naming angles, reading a protractor, angles in a right angle, on a straight line and around a point, vertically opposite angles, and complementary and supplementary angles. Expected adds reflex angles, angle pairs on parallel lines (naming them, finding angles, and deciding whether lines are parallel), and multi-step problems and equations with reasons.

integers.subtitle: Basic covers integers on a number line, comparing and ordering, thermometers, adding and subtracting, multiplying and dividing, and problems in context. Expected adds why a negative times a negative is positive, chains of multiplication and division, order of operations, substitution with negatives, reasoning (true or false, spot the error) and multi-part problems.

equations.subtitle: Basic covers representing equations, balances and bar models, solving by inspection, one-step and two-step equations, word problems, checking by substitution and solving x² = c. Expected adds fraction and bracket equations, collecting like terms, pronumerals on both sides, equivalent equations, formulas, form-solve-check, spotting errors, multi-step word problems and ax² = c.

fdp.subtitle: Basic covers equivalent and simplified fractions, comparing, rounding, terminating and recurring decimals, conversions, rational and irrational numbers, ordering, adding and subtracting, fractions of quantities and sets, and percentages of quantities. Expected adds mixed numbers, multiplying and dividing fractions and decimals, one quantity as a percentage of another, percentage change, discounts, GST, profit and loss, reverse percentages, the double number line and reasoning.

s3-whole-numbers.topic: Represents Numbers: Whole Numbers and Integers
s3-whole-numbers.subtitle: Part A: recognise, represent and order numbers in the millions; apply place value to partition, regroup and rename numbers to 1 billion. Parts A and B add: locate and represent integers on a number line.

s3-decimals.subtitle: Part A: recognise that the place value system can be extended beyond hundredths; compare, order and represent decimals.

s3-percentages.subtitle: Part B: make connections between benchmark fractions, decimals and percentages; determine percentage discounts of 10%, 25% and 50%.

s3-additive.subtitle: Part A: apply efficient mental and written strategies to solve addition and subtraction problems; use estimation and place value understanding to determine the reasonableness of solutions. Parts A and B add: choose and use efficient strategies to solve addition and subtraction problems; applies known strategies to add and subtract decimals.

s3-multiply-divide.subtitle: Part A: determine products and factors; use partitioning and place value to multiply 2-, 3- and 4-digit numbers by one-digit numbers; select and apply mental and written strategies to multiply 2- and 3-digit numbers by 2-digit numbers; represent and solve division problems with whole number remainders; select and apply strategies to divide a number with 3 or more digits by a one-digit divisor; use estimation and rounding to check the reasonableness of answers to calculations. Parts A and B add: select and apply strategies to solve problems involving multiplication and division with whole numbers; multiply and divide decimals by powers of 10.

s3-number-sentences.topic: Multiplicative Relations: Number Sentences and Patterns
s3-number-sentences.subtitle: Part B: use equivalent number sentences involving multiplication and division to find unknown quantities; represent and describe number patterns formed by multiples; explore the use of brackets and the order of operations to write number sentences.

s3-fractions.subtitle: Part A: recognise the role of the number 1 as representing the whole; compare and order common unit fractions; solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions with the same denominator. Parts A and B add: recognise that a fraction can represent a division; compare common fractions with related denominators; use equivalence to add and subtract fractional quantities.

s3-fraction-quantities.subtitle: Part B: build up to the whole from a given fractional part; find fractional quantities of whole numbers (halves, quarters, fifths and tenths).

s3-position.subtitle: Part A: explore the Cartesian coordinate system. Parts A and B add: use the 4 quadrants of the coordinate plane.

s3-length.subtitle: Part A: use metres and kilometres for length and distances; measure lengths to find perimeters. Parts A and B add: connect decimal representations to the metric system; convert between common metric units of length; solve problems involving the comparison of lengths using appropriate units.

s3-angles.subtitle: Part A: estimate, measure and compare angles using degrees; use a protractor to measure and identify types of angles. Parts A and B add: investigate angles on a straight line and angles at a point; investigate the relationships formed by the intersection of straight lines.

s3-2d-shapes.subtitle: Part A: classify two-dimensional shapes and describe their properties. Parts A and B add: dissect two-dimensional shapes and rearrange them using translations, reflections and rotations.

s3-area-rectangles.subtitle: Part A: use hectares and square kilometres as units of measurement for area; calculate the areas of rectangles using familiar metric units.

s3-area-composite.topic: 2D Spatial Structure: Area of Composite Figures, Parallelograms and Triangles
s3-area-composite.subtitle: Part B: find the area of composite figures; calculate the area of a parallelogram using subdivision and rearrangement; determine the area of a triangle.

s3-3d-objects.subtitle: Part A: compare, describe and name prisms and pyramids; connect three-dimensional objects with two-dimensional representations. Parts A and B add: construct prisms and pyramids.

s3-volume-capacity.subtitle: Part A: choose appropriate units of measurement for capacity; use displacement to investigate volumes of irregular solids; connect decimal representations to the metric system. Parts A and B add: use cubic metres for measurement of volume; recognise the multiplicative structure for finding volume; find the volumes of rectangular prisms in cubic centimetres and cubic metres.

s3-mass.subtitle: Part A: choose appropriate units of measurement for mass; connect decimal representations to the metric system. Parts A and B add: convert between common metric units of mass.

s3-time.subtitle: Part A: compare 12- and 24-hour time systems and convert between them. Parts A and B add: solve problems involving duration, using 12- and 24-hour time.

s3-data-collect.subtitle: Part A: collect categorical and discrete numerical data by observation or survey; choose and use appropriate tables and graphs.

s3-data-interpret.subtitle: Part A: describe and interpret different datasets in context. Parts A and B add: interpret and compare a range of data displays; interpret data presented in digital media and elsewhere.

s3-chance.subtitle: Part A: list outcomes of chance experiments involving equally likely outcomes and represent probabilities. Parts A and B add: compare observed frequencies of outcomes with expected results; create random generators and describe probabilities using fractions; conduct chance experiments with both small and large numbers of trials.

length.subtitle: Basic covers the perimeter of parallelograms, trapeziums, rhombuses, kites and composite figures, the parts of a circle and the circumference from the radius or diameter. Expected adds composite figures with sides to find, arc length, the perimeter of sectors, semicircles and quadrants, composite figures with curves, and working backwards from a circumference.

algebraic-techniques.subtitle: Basic covers coefficients, pronumerals and constants, algebraic notation, writing expressions from words, one-step substitution, collecting like terms, multiplying and dividing a term, expanding a bracket and factorising out a number. Expected adds tables of values, multi-step expressions from words, two-step substitution and substitution with two pronumerals, mixed like terms, multiplying terms, algebraic fractions, expanding and simplifying, and factorising with negatives, two pronumerals and three terms.

s5-financial-mathematics-a.topic: Financial Mathematics A: Earning, Spending and Simple Interest
s5-financial-mathematics-a.subtitle: Core outcome. Solve problems involving earning money; solve problems involving simple interest; solve problems involving spending money. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding pay rises and percentage change, leave loading, taxable income, tax payable from the resident tax table, net earnings after deductions and tax and more.

s5-financial-mathematics-b.topic: Financial Mathematics B: Compound Interest and Depreciation
s5-financial-mathematics-b.subtitle: Core outcome. Solve problems involving compound interest and depreciation. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding compound interest with different compounding periods, compare simple interest and compound interest, calculate the amount to invest now, calculate rate or time in compound situations, calculate rate or time in depreciation situations.

s5-algebraic-techniques-a.topic: Algebraic Techniques A: Algebraic Fractions and Expanding
s5-algebraic-techniques-a.subtitle: Core outcome. Apply the 4 operations to simplify algebraic fractions with numerical denominators; apply the distributive law to the expansion of algebraic expressions, and collect like terms where appropriate. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding mixed algebraic fraction operations, factorise by taking out a negative common factor, expand two separate brackets and simplify, expand binomial products, expand binomial products using an area model and more.

s5-algebraic-techniques-b.topic: Algebraic Techniques B: Factorising and Binomial Products
s5-algebraic-techniques-b.subtitle: Path outcome. Apply the 4 operations involving algebraic fractions with pronumerals in the denominator; factorise algebraic expressions by taking out a common algebraic factor; expand binomial products and factorise monic quadratic expressions. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding add and subtract algebraic fractions (pronumeral denominators), factorise: a common binomial factor, expand and simplify, multi-part expand and factorise problem.

s5-algebraic-techniques-c.topic: Algebraic Techniques C: Special Products and Factorising
s5-algebraic-techniques-c.subtitle: Path outcome. Operate with algebraic fractions involving binomial numerators and numerical denominators; expand, factorise and simplify algebraic expressions including special products. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding factorise by grouping in pairs, factorise non-monic quadratics, factorise completely (common factor first), complete the square, factorise: choose the technique and more.

s5-indices-a.topic: Indices A: Index Laws, Zero and Negative Indices
s5-indices-a.subtitle: Core outcome. Extend and apply the index laws to variables, using positive-integer indices and the zero index; simplify algebraic products and quotients using index laws; apply index laws to numerical expressions with negative-integer indices. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding power of a quotient, simplify fractions with indices, substitute into expressions with indices, multi-part index laws problem, index laws with negative numerical indices and more.

s5-indices-b.topic: Indices B: Negative Indices in Algebra
s5-indices-b.subtitle: Path outcome. Apply index laws to algebraic expressions involving negative-integer indices. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding powers of powers with negative indices, a fraction to a negative power, simplify algebraic fractions with negative indices, evaluate by substitution, multi-part negative indices problem.

s5-indices-c.topic: Indices C: Surds and Fractional Indices
s5-indices-c.subtitle: Path outcome. Describe surds; apply knowledge of surds to solve problems; describe and use fractional indices. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding compare and order surds, expand brackets with surds, binomial products with surds, rationalise the denominator, rationalise a binomial denominator and more.

s5-equations-a.subtitle: Core outcome. Solve linear equations involving up to 3 steps; solve linear equations involving one algebraic fraction; solve linear equations arising from word problems and substitution into formulas. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding equations with decimals, mixed linear equations up to 3 steps, pronumerals on both sides with constants, pronumerals on both sides with negative terms, equations involving brackets on both sides and more.

s5-equations-b.topic: Equations B: Quadratics, Cubics and Inequalities
s5-equations-b.subtitle: Path outcome. Solve monic quadratic equations; solve cubic equations; solve linear inequalities and graph their solutions on a number line. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding solve (x + a)² = k, rearrange, then solve, quadratic equations from problems, inequalities: dividing by a negative, inequalities from worded problems and more.

s5-equations-c.topic: Equations C: Literal, Quadratic and Simultaneous Equations
s5-equations-c.subtitle: Path outcome. Solve linear equations involving algebraic fractions and equations of more than 3 steps; rearrange literal equations; solve quadratic equations using a variety of methods; solve linear simultaneous equations, both algebraically and graphically. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding solve by completing the square, how many solutions? (the discriminant), quadratic equations in context, simultaneous equations from problems, multi-part equations problem.

s5-linear-relationships-a.topic: Linear Relationships A: Midpoint, Gradient and Distance
s5-linear-relationships-a.subtitle: Core outcome. Find the midpoint and gradient of a line segment (interval) on the Cartesian plane; find the distance between 2 points located on the Cartesian plane; recognise and graph equations; examine parallel, horizontal and vertical lines. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding find an endpoint from the midpoint, gradient as a slope in context, multi-part interval problem.

s5-linear-relationships-b.subtitle: Core outcome. Examine the gradient/slope-intercept form; find the equations of parallel and perpendicular lines. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding rearrange into y = mx + c, equation from a point and the gradient, equation through two points, interpret m and c in context, multi-part straight-line problem and more.

s5-linear-relationships-c.topic: Linear Relationships C: Coordinate Geometry and Transformations
s5-linear-relationships-c.subtitle: Path outcome. Apply formulas to find the midpoint and gradient/slope of an interval on the Cartesian plane; apply the distance formula to find the distance between 2 points located on the Cartesian plane; use various forms of the equation of a straight line; solve problems by applying coordinate geometry formulas; identify line and rotational symmetries; describe translations, reflections in an axis, and rotations through multiples of 90 degrees on the Cartesian plane, using coordinates. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding are the points collinear?, line through two points in general form, the perpendicular bisector of an interval, prove a triangle is right-angled or isosceles, prove a quadrilateral is a parallelogram and more.

s5-non-linear-relationships-a.topic: Non-Linear Relationships A: Tables and Graphs
s5-non-linear-relationships-a.subtitle: Core outcome. Examine the connection between algebraic and graphical representations of quadratics and exponentials. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding graph a quadratic from a table of values, graph an exponential from a table of values, match simple curves to equations, use table patterns to identify relationship type.

s5-non-linear-relationships-b.topic: Non-Linear Relationships B: Parabolas and Exponential Curves
s5-non-linear-relationships-b.subtitle: Core outcome. Graph and examine quadratic relationships; graph and examine exponential relationships; distinguish between linear, quadratic and exponential relationships by examining their graphical representations. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding solve a linear-quadratic pair using a graph, solve a linear-exponential pair using a graph, match graphs with linear, quadratic and exponential equations, solve simple real-life non-linear relationship problems.

s5-non-linear-relationships-c.topic: Non-Linear Relationships C: Parabolas, Hyperbolas, Circles and More
s5-non-linear-relationships-c.subtitle: Path outcome. Graph parabolas and describe their features and transformations; graph exponentials and describe their features and transformations; graph hyperbolas and describe their features and transformations; graph circles and describe their features and transformations; distinguish between different types of graphs by examining their algebraic and graphical representations and solve problems; graph and compare polynomial curves and describe their features and transformations. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding complete the square to find the vertex, find a parabola's equation from its graph, circles: complete the square, is a point inside, on or outside a circle?, intersection of a line and a curve.

s5-variation-a.topic: Variation and Rates of Change A: Direct and Inverse Variation
s5-variation-a.subtitle: Path outcome. Identify and describe problems involving direct and inverse variation; identify and describe graphs involving direct and inverse variation; solve problems involving direct and inverse variation and examine the relationship between graphs and equations corresponding to proportionality. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding inverse variation in context, effect of changing x on y, variation with powers (y ∝ x², 1/x², …), multi-part variation problem.

s5-variation-b.topic: Variation and Rates of Change B: Rates of Change
s5-variation-b.subtitle: Path outcome. Analyse graphs that are decreasing or increasing at a constant rate; analyse the relationship between graphs and variable rates of change; construct graphical representations of rates of change. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding travel graphs: interpret the journey, compare two rates on one graph, average rate of change from a curve, multi-part rates problem.

s5-polynomials.subtitle: Path outcome. Define and operate with polynomials; divide polynomials; apply the factor and remainder theorems to solve problems; graph polynomials. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding multiply polynomials, find an unknown coefficient, factorise a cubic, solve a cubic equation, find a polynomial's equation from its graph.

s5-logarithms.subtitle: Path outcome. Examine logarithms both numerically and graphically; establish and apply the laws of logarithms to solve problems. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding the graph of y = logₐ x, true or false? Log statements, expand using the log laws, express in terms of given logs, solve logarithmic equations and more.

s5-functions-graphs.subtitle: Path outcome. Define relations and functions, and use function notation; find the domain and range of a function and graph functions; graph regions corresponding to linear inequalities in one and 2 variables. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding substitute expressions into f(x), solve f(x) = k, multi-part function problem, write the inequality for a region, regions with more than one inequality.

s5-numbers-of-any-magnitude.subtitle: Core outcome. Identify and describe very small and very large measurements; find absolute and percentage error; estimate and round numbers to a specified degree of accuracy; express numbers in scientific notation. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding very large and very small quantities in context, upper and lower bounds in calculations, compare and order numbers in scientific notation, calculate with scientific notation, multi-part scientific notation problem.

s5-trigonometry-a.subtitle: Core outcome. Demonstrate and explain the constancy of trigonometric ratios for a given angle in right-angled triangles; apply trigonometry to solve right-angled triangle problems. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding approximate trig ratios for a given angle, trigonometry with degrees and minutes, practical right-triangle problems, use Pythagoras, then write a trig ratio, two right-angled triangles sharing a side and more.

s5-trigonometry-b.topic: Trigonometry B: Elevation, Depression and Bearings
s5-trigonometry-b.subtitle: Core outcome. Solve right-angled triangle problems involving angles of elevation and depression; solve right-angled triangle problems involving bearings. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding work backwards to find reverse bearings, solve practical bearing problems with a diagram, solve practical bearing problems by drawing a diagram, find a distance using bearings, find a bearing using trigonometry and more.

s5-trigonometry-c.topic: Trigonometry C: Non-Right-Angled Triangles and 3D Problems
s5-trigonometry-c.subtitle: Path outcome. Solve 3-dimensional problems involving right-angled triangles; apply the sine, cosine and area rules to any triangle and solve related problems. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding 3D bearings and elevation/depression applications, multi-step 3D practical problems, sine rule — find an unknown angle, cosine rule — find an unknown angle, choose sine, cosine or area rule.

s5-trigonometry-d.topic: Trigonometry D: The Unit Circle and Trigonometric Equations
s5-trigonometry-d.subtitle: Path outcome. Use the unit circle to define trigonometric functions and represent them graphically; solve trigonometric equations using exact values and the relationships between supplementary and complementary angles. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding exact values for angles of any magnitude, given one ratio and the quadrant, find the others, features of trigonometric graphs, identify the trigonometric graph (A–D), solve trigonometric equations (exact) and more.

s5-area-and-surface-area-a.topic: Area and Surface Area A: Composite Areas, Prisms and Cylinders
s5-area-and-surface-area-a.subtitle: Core outcome. Solve problems involving areas and surface areas; develop and apply the formula for surface areas of cylinders; solve problems involving surface areas of cylinders and related composite solids. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding surface area of trapezoidal prisms, surface area of composite prisms, practical area applications, surface area of composite solids involving cylinders, practical cylinder surface area problems.

s5-area-and-surface-area-b.topic: Area and Surface Area B: Pyramids, Cones and Spheres
s5-area-and-surface-area-b.subtitle: Path outcome. Solve problems involving surface areas. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding pyramid: find the slant height first, rectangular-based pyramid, cone: find the slant height first, composite solids, find a dimension from the surface area and more.

s5-volume-a.topic: Volume A: Prisms, Cylinders and Composite Solids
s5-volume-a.subtitle: Core outcome. Solve problems involving composite solids consisting of right prisms and cylinders. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding find a missing dimension from the volume, cylinders: find the radius or height, composite prisms, part-circle prisms, composite cylinders and more.

s5-volume-b.topic: Volume B: Pyramids, Cones and Spheres
s5-volume-b.subtitle: Path outcome. Solve problems involving volumes. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding pyramid volume from the slant height, cone volume from the slant height, volume of composite solids, solids with a part removed, find a dimension from the volume and more.

s5-geometrical-figures-a.topic: Properties of Geometrical Figures A: Similar Figures and Scale
s5-geometrical-figures-a.subtitle: Core outcome. Identify and describe the properties of similar figures; solve problems using ratio and scale factors in similar figures. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding similar triangles with a parallel side, find two unknown sides, find the scale of a drawing, shadows and heights, areas and volumes of similar figures.

s5-geometrical-figures-b.topic: Properties of Geometrical Figures B: Congruence, Similarity and Reasoning
s5-geometrical-figures-b.subtitle: Path outcome. Identify and explain congruence; develop and use the conditions for congruent triangles; develop and apply the minimum conditions for triangles to be similar; establish and apply properties of similar shapes and solids; apply logical reasoning to numerical problems involving plane shapes. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding why SSA and AAA are not tests, find two unknown sides, exterior angles of triangles and polygons.

s5-geometrical-figures-c.topic: Properties of Geometrical Figures C: Geometric Proofs
s5-geometrical-figures-c.subtitle: Path outcome. Apply logical reasoning to proofs involving plane shapes. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding prove congruent, then deduce a property, prove two triangles similar, then find a length, prove a property of a quadrilateral, prove a property of an isosceles triangle.

s5-circle-geometry.subtitle: Path outcome. Prove and apply angle and chord properties of circles; prove and apply tangent and secant properties of circles. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding cyclic quadrilaterals, exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral, intersecting chords, the alternate segment theorem, secants and tangents from an external point.

s5-introduction-to-networks.subtitle: Path outcome. Examine and describe a graph/network; define a planar graph and apply Euler’s formula for planar graphs; explain the concept of Eulerian trails and circuits in the context of the Königsberg bridges problem. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding same graph drawn in different ways, length of a route in a weighted network, shortest path in a weighted network.

s5-data-analysis-a.topic: Data Analysis A: Quartiles, Box Plots and Standard Deviation
s5-data-analysis-a.subtitle: Core outcome. Examine standard deviation as a measure of spread; determine quartiles and interquartile range; represent datasets using box plots and use them to compare datasets. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding effect of changes on mean, median and SD, quartiles from a stem-and-leaf plot, identify outliers (1.5 × IQR), compare parallel box plots, skewness and shape and more.

s5-data-analysis-b.subtitle: Core outcome. Identify and describe numerical datasets involving 2 variables; represent datasets involving 2 numerical variables, using a scatter plot and a line of best fit, by eye; interpret data involving 2 numerical variables, using graphical representations. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding association and causation, equation of a line of best fit, outliers in bivariate data.

s5-data-analysis-c.topic: Data Analysis C: Statistical Inquiries and Media Reports
s5-data-analysis-c.subtitle: Path outcome. Plan and conduct a statistical inquiry into a question of interest; examine reports of studies in digital media and elsewhere for information on their planning and implementation. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding calculate a stratified sample, systematic sampling, plan a statistical inquiry, evaluate a claim in a report.

s5-probability-a.subtitle: Core outcome. Describe multistage chance experiments involving independent and dependent events; solve problems for multistage chance experiments; design and use simulations to model and examine situations involving probability. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding with or without replacement?, at least one (complement), three-stage experiments.

s5-probability-b.topic: Probability B: Venn Diagrams, Two-Way Tables and Conditional Probability
s5-probability-b.subtitle: Path outcome. Solve problems involving Venn diagrams and 2-way tables; use the language, 'if … then', 'given', 'of' and 'knowing that', to examine conditional statements and identify common mistakes in interpreting the language; describe mutually and non-mutually exclusive events using specific language and calculate related probabilities. Basic keeps to the first steps of each content statement; Expected is the whole outcome, adding three-set Venn diagrams, two-way tables and Venn diagrams.
